newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - JUNE 5.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - JUNE 5.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
-- The government plans to amend the law listing the assets which have to be retained in state ownership.
-- The government discusses a plan to replace the one-level school maturity exam system with a two-level one.
-- The chief prosecutor of Budapest initiated an investigation on how information about handling a privatisation corruption case leaked to the press.
-- The parliament continues to discuss the draft justice reform law.
-- No one injured in an unprecedented series of bombings Thursday morning, in which four explosions happened within a few hours in Budapest.
-- The Government Supervision Office (KEI) initiated legal action against an investment company which had not accounted for the whereabouts of compensation coupons of billions of forints.
